samples.summary: Unrelated scope creep: a CI lane-selection test fix is bundled into a CLI dry-run/URL-encoding change. The rewrite of the `resolve fail-safes` case (adding `GITHUB_EVENT_NAME`/`GITHUB_REF_NAME` and a `push to main` assertion) has nothing to do with `--dry-run` on read commands or path-segment encoding, and it changes what that fail-safe test proves (it no longer exercises the bare empty-string fall-through). It belongs in its own change so it can be reviewed on its own merits.

`seg()` folds the *empty* segment into the traversal rejection, but an empty workspace is a documented, expected configuration state, not an attack. `resolveConfig` deliberately returns `workspace: ''` when no `--workspace`/`WAFFLEBASE_WORKSPACE`/profile value exists (packages/cli/src/config/config.ts:100,126,146,164) and the comment at config.ts:108 explicitly anticipates `/workspaces//...` yielding a 404. After this change every command — including `--dry-run` previews — dies with `Invalid identifier "": a URL path segment cannot be empty, "." or ".." — the URL parser resolves those...`, which misdescribes the situation (nothing was "named") and hides the real cause (no workspace configured / not logged in). The dot-segment defence does not require conflating the two cases; a distinct "no workspace configured" error is what the CLI's error taxonomy (docs/design/cli.md §8.1 exit codes) implies.

The change's stated invariant — "the preview is the request" via a single shared builder (`client/url.ts`, and the doc text at docs/design/cli.md:839-845) — is not applied to the two commands whose paths are non-trivial. `cells get`'s three-way endpoint selection and range encoding are re-implemented in commands/cells.ts:25-30, and the same query encoding again in commands/sheets-export.ts:47-55, duplicating the logic that already lives in `HttpClient.getCells`/`getCell` (http-client.ts:345-357). These are exactly the cases where preview and request can drift, and the fix (expose a path builder from the client, as was done for `apiKeysUrl`) is the pattern the change itself establishes elsewhere.

Doc claim is stated absolutely but is only true of network requests: "The one command the flag does not hold back is `login`". `logout` (packages/cli/src/commands/logout.ts:9) clears the session file and `ctx switch` (commands/ctx.ts:71-73) rewrites it, both ignoring `--dry-run`. Either scope the sentence to requests or list these local mutations.

Doc structure: the `import` / `upload` envelope-variation sentence is spliced mid-paragraph into the dot-segment rejection bullet, so an unrelated topic (envelope shape of import previews) is buried inside a security-rationale paragraph. It should be its own bullet next to the existing `docs import` bullets at cli.md:866-869.

Consolidation left behind: `origin()` in url.ts:44 is private, so the trailing-slash strip it replaced still exists verbatim in `refreshSession` (http-client.ts:96) and in commands/login.ts:36,56,75,92, which build `${server}/auth/...` and `${server}/workspaces` by hand. If the point is one definition of how a request URL is formed, these non-v1 URLs should go through the same module (or at least reuse `origin()`).

Inconsistent placement of the new dry-run branches: `docs get` (docs.ts:126) and `tabs list` (tabs.ts:15) preview *outside* the surrounding try/catch, while notes/slides/files/api-keys place theirs inside. Since `seg()` now throws, the same bad identifier surfaces as an `outputError` envelope in some namespaces and as an unhandled throw escaping to `runCli` in others — the branch's own test acknowledges this (test/read-dry-run.test.ts:313-316). Pick one placement so the error envelope and exit code are uniform per docs/design/cli.md §8.1.

`detectFormat(file, localOpts.fileFormat);` is called purely for its throwing side effect and the result discarded, which reads as dead code. Prefer assigning it (and reusing the value below) or a named `assertSupportedFormat()` so the intent survives future edits.

The rewrite of the `resolve fail-safes` case (adding `GITHUB_EVENT_NAME`/`GITHUB_REF_NAME` and a `push to main` assertion) has nothing to do with `--dry-run` on read commands or path-segment encoding, and it changes what that fail-safe test proves (it no longer exercises the bare empty-string fall-through). It belongs in its own change so it can be reviewed on its own merits.

verdict.reason: The edit exists but is not a blocking design-fit violation. (a) It is not unrelated: `resolve()` with no GITHUB_EVENT_NAME falls back to merge-base against main (scripts/changed-areas.mjs:314-323) and feeds the result to classify (:545-553); @wafflebase/cli is a graphed workspace package (packages/cli/package.json:2), so a CLI-only diff classifies as full:false and the OLD bare `resolve({WAFFLEBASE_CHANGED_AREAS:""})` assertion fails on precisely this branch — the env keys are a forced fix, not free-floating creep. (b) The stated harm is overstated: the new `/push to main/` assertion (scripts/test/changed-areas.test.mjs:730) is reachable only if the empty string was ignored by the guard at scripts/changed-areas.mjs:510 (otherwise JSON.parse("") throws and returns the "not valid JSON" reason at :513-515), so the empty-string fall-through is still pinned, more tightly than the old assertion which any full-run route satisfied. (c) The remedy asked for — "belongs in its own change" — is PR-splitting hygiene, which this rubric classifies as minor/taste and which never blocks; it cites no acceptance criterion, no missing or parallel design doc, no duplicated module, no stated Non-Goal. The substantive residue (the test short-circuits at the gate) is test quality, explicitly out of the design-fit lane, and the test-adequacy lens already filed it as minor non-blocking (.agent-review/test-adequacy/summary.md:17). Only the pre-existing `push to main is never filtered` test at :223-230 is separately attributed as pre-existing by the file's own note at :656-660.

finding.summary: `seg()` folds the *empty* segment into the traversal rejection, but an empty workspace is a documented, expected configuration state, not an attack. `resolveConfig` deliberately returns `workspace: ''` when no `--workspace`/`WAFFLEBASE_WORKSPACE`/profile value exists (packages/cli/src/config/config.ts:100,126,146,164) and the comment at config.ts:108 explicitly anticipates `/workspaces//...` yielding a 404. After this change every command — including `--dry-run` previews — dies with `Invalid identifier "": a URL path segment cannot be empty, "." or ".." — the URL parser resolves those...`, which misdescribes the situation (nothing was "named") and hides the real cause (no workspace configured / not logged in). The dot-segment defence does not require conflating the two cases; a distinct "no workspace configured" error is what the CLI's error taxonomy (docs/design/cli.md §8.1 exit codes) implies.

verdict.reason: The code is present as described. `seg()` (packages/cli/src/client/url.ts:31-41) rejects the empty segment in the same branch and with the same traversal-framed message as the dot-segment case. `config.workspace` flows through `seg()` in both URL builders (url.ts:50, url.ts:61), and `resolveConfig` deliberately defaults `workspace` to `''` in all four branches (config/config.ts:100,126,147,164), with the comment at config.ts:106-110 explicitly treating the empty workspace as an expected state that yields a `/workspaces//...` 404 — so the two conditions really are conflated. Nothing guards the path: `printDryRun` calls `apiV1Base(config)` with no workspace precheck (client/dry-run.ts:18) and `HttpClient.base` does the same (client/http-client.ts:86-88); grep found no `no workspace configured` check anywhere in packages/cli/src. On the spec side this is in-lane rather than mere message taste: the originating task's acceptance criterion (docs/tasks/active/20260816-cli-dry-run-read-commands-todo.md:56-60) requires the `--dry-run` envelope to print and exit 0 in a bare `WAFFLEBASE_SERVER=http://127.0.0.1:1` environment, which the new empty-segment throw breaks when no workspace is configured. The design doc does mention "or empty" as rejected (docs/design/cli.md:851-857), but that text is part of the same change and does not resolve the conflation; §8.1 (cli.md:805-807) offers no distinct code either, so only the taxonomy half of the argument is weak. No named refutation ground (not-present / already-guarded / out-of-scope) holds.

verdict.reason: The duplication is present as described (cells.ts:21-33 re-derives the three-way endpoint + range encoding; sheets-export.ts:45-56 re-derives the query; http-client.ts:345-357 holds the same logic), but it is not a blocking fit violation under this lens. (a) The invariant the change actually states is about identifier encoding and the shared base, not per-endpoint path builders: docs/design/cli.md:843-850 says "one `seg()` in `client/url.ts`, used by both", and both cited sites use `seg()` plus the shared `apiV1Base` via `printDryRun` (client/dry-run.ts:12-19). `apiKeysUrl` is explicitly documented (url.ts:53-59, dry-run.ts:21-26, cli.md:838-842) as an exception forced by routes that sit outside the v1 base and therefore cannot be expressed as a `printDryRun` path — not as a pattern every command must follow. (b) Inlining the path with `seg()` is the uniform, documented mechanism at all 36 `printDryRun` call sites across 8 command files; asking two of them to hoist a 3-line template into a builder is a "could be cleaner" refactor preference (minor, never blocks), and the duplicated unit is a template expression, not an existing module. (c) The documented acceptance behavior for these commands (cli.md:862-864: `?range=` / `/cells/A1` / `/cells`) is satisfied, and preview vs request are pinned to identical URLs by test/http-client-paths.test.ts:71 and test/read-dry-run.test.ts:164,175, so no acceptance criterion is unmet and no drift exists today.
